name: Sheleph
overview: Sheleph is a male figure mentioned in the Bible as the son of Joktan, as recorded in Genesis 10:26. Beyond this paternal link, Scripture provides no additional details about his tribe or other distinguishing attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Sheleph means 'one plucked out, drawn out,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with no indication that it was given directly by God. This meaning may imply a sense of separation or selection, but the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Sheleph is identified as the son of Joktan, establishing his place within Joktan's lineage. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for Sheleph beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Sheleph's significance in the biblical narrative lies primarily in his genealogical placement as a descendant of Joktan. This connection situates him within the broader framework of post-Flood humanity's expansion and the unfolding of God's providential plan through generations. While the Bible does not provide further details about his life or role, his mention contributes to the historical record of God's people.
